candidate_identity.candidate: standardized symmetric four-corner RIPr/numeraire candidate for the frozen NIG Gaussian block predictor

classification.protocol_matched_external_replication: C/not applicable to this unpublished adaptation; none located
classification.promotion_status: BLOCKED until analytic or interval-certified continuum constraint

published_or_primary_support.source: Larsson, Ramdas & Ruf, The numeraire e-variable and reverse information projection, arXiv:2402.18810
published_or_primary_support.support: For a point alternative Q versus composite null P, the numeraire exists and is log-optimal. Theorem 4.7 gives the RIPr verification condition E_Q[p/p*] <= 1 for every null density p. Section 7 shows the RIPr density is pointwise <= the null likelihood envelope p_max, hence the numeraire q/p* pointwise dominates universal inference q/p_max.

published_or_primary_support.source: Grunwald, de Heide & Koolen, Safe Testing
published_or_primary_support.support: Conditional e-values can be multiplied under optional continuation; this supports blockwise reuse once the frozen-reference factor is itself conditionally e-valid.
Provides the finite-sample composite-null likelihood-envelope baseline represented here by q/p_max.

exact_standardization_constants.result: Matches source certificate to displayed precision.

independent_reconstruction.location_scale_check: Under y=(Y-Xbar_R)/s_R, both the NIG joint predictive with beta0=2*s_R^2 and every Gaussian null block density acquire exactly the same s_R^{-m} factor, so their ratio is reference-scale free. The confidence rectangle becomes the single standardized rectangle [-h0,h0] x [ell0,u0].

deterministic_quadrature.method: Independent implementation of 50-point generalized Gauss-Laguerre for tau=1/sigma^2 ~ Gamma(3, rate=2), 60-point Gauss-Hermite for the standardized block mean, and 50-point generalized Gauss-Laguerre for chi-square residual SSE; m=32.
deterministic_quadrature.result: Reproduced the reported active-pair root and log-growth numbers to displayed precision without worker code.

independent_monte_carlo.result: Independent stochastic validation is consistent with the deterministic values; it is not a safety certificate.

continuum_search.method: Independent differential-evolution search over mu in [0,h0], sigma in [ell0,u0] against the deterministic quadrature objective C(mu,sigma)=E_q[p_mu,sigma/p_rho], using symmetry mu>=0 and seed 12345.
continuum_search.status: Strong numerical corner-max evidence only. Differential evolution plus finite-order quadrature is not an analytic or directed-rounding proof of sup C<=1.

scope_and_failures: The candidate is a worker adaptation, not a published four-corner construction from the cited papers. Primary literature supports the numeraire/RIPr criterion and pointwise UI dominance, not this specific rho or corner support.

The independent reconstruction strongly reproduces rho and the ~1.04289 nat/block expected-log gain, but exact e-validity still requires C(mu,sigma)<=1 over the entire continuous standardized Gaussian rectangle.

Because the active corner constraints equal one, an uncertified numerical optimizer has essentially no safety margin. Floating-point agreement at the corners cannot substitute for interval/analytic coverage of the interior and boundary.
If only sup C <= 1+epsilon can be certified, q/((1+epsilon)p_rho) is the defensible e-factor; the effect of scaling on pointwise dominance over q/p_max must then be checked explicitly.
No heavy-tail, serial-dependence, gradual-drift, repeated-change, non-Gaussian-reference, or unfrozen-predictive guarantee follows.
The C18 downstream identity-contract blocker is orthogonal to this audit; this result binds directly to the exact source artifact tuple and does not repair or reinterpret comparator identity rows.

decision.what_is_supported: The exact standardization reduction, theoretical numeraire criterion, four-corner mixture root, and claimed expected-log improvement are reproducible and internally coherent at high numerical precision.
decision.what_is_not_supported: Promotion of q/p_rho as a valid e-factor/RIPr/numeraire is not yet justified because the continuum constraint is not machine/analytic certified.
decision.recommended_use: Treat the four-corner factor as a high-priority candidate for rigorous certification, not as a production-safe replacement.

exact_next_action: Certify C(mu,sigma)=E_q[p_mu,sigma/p_rho]<=1 on mu in [0,h0], sigma in [ell0,u0] using an analytic corner-max proof or directed-rounding interval cover. Reuse symmetry and sufficient-statistic quadrature only as discovery guidance. If the best certified bound is 1+epsilon, scale by 1+epsilon and verify whether q/((1+epsilon)p_rho) still pointwise dominates q/p_max on the standardized domain. Do not re-audit unchanged numerical evidence.
